A.topic: #39 How to set up a small nursery

ig.text:
No spare room for a nursery? Good news: you don't need one yet. Your baby sleeps in your room for the first six months, so the real job is a safe sleep space that fits beside your bed.
👉 Swipe for 7 space-saving moves that stay safe, from the right wall for the cot to the one piece of furniture you can skip.
📌 Save this before you move a single thing.
🔗 Compare crib prices from UK shops: link in bio.
#ukmums #pregnancyuk #nurseryuk #newparentsuk #firsttimemumuk

pin.text: No spare room? For the first six months your baby sleeps in your room, so start with a bedside crib or mini cot. Keep the cot away from radiators, blind cords and the window, change nappies on the floor, fix tall furniture to the wall and keep the room at 16 to 20°C. Compare crib prices from UK shops at BabySorted. Source: The Lullaby Trust, the UK safer baby sleep charity, RoSPA, the UK accident prevention charity, and NHS.

descendants.text: Safe sleep setup checklist for a newborn nursery https://babysorted.com/article?slug=safe-sleep-setup-checklist

th.text:
No spare room for a nursery? You don't need one yet. For the first six months your baby sleeps in your room anyway.
1. Bedside crib or mini cot, with a mattress that fits with no gaps.
2. Cot away from radiators, sunlight, blind cords and the window.
3. Skip the changing table: change nappies on a mat on the floor.
4. Fix tall furniture to the wall.
Source: The Lullaby Trust, RoSPA and NHS

Thinking about a formula prep machine? Check one thing first.
The NHS says formula should be made with water at 70°C or more, because powder isn't sterile, even in a sealed tin.
If you use a machine, make sure the water that comes out is at least 70°C when it mixes with the powder. Test it with a digital food thermometer. Too cool? Stop using it and make feeds by hand.

E.topic: #43 Rear-facing for longer: why experts recommend it

ig.text:
Turning your child forward at 15 months is legal. But it's the floor, not the goal.
The reason safety experts say "keep them rear-facing" comes down to one surprising number about a baby's head.
👉 Swipe for the science, the law and the worry about legs you can drop.
📌 Save it for when someone asks why you haven't turned the seat yet.
🔗 Compare car seat prices from UK shops: link in bio.
#carseatsafetyuk #rearfacinguk #ukmums #toddlermumuk #newparentsuk

pin.text: A baby's head is about a quarter of their body weight, so a rear-facing seat protects the head and neck far better in a frontal crash. UK law says rear-facing until over 15 months for R129 seats, and many seats go rear-facing to about 4 years. Bent legs are fine. Never fit one in front of a live airbag. Compare car seat prices from UK shops at BabySorted. Source: RoSPA, the UK accident prevention charity, and GOV.UK.
mediaAltText: Smiling baby in a striped hat waving on a fluffy rug above six reasons to stay rear-facing with a black extended rear-facing car seat, on white.

pinterestData.pinTitle: Rear-Facing for Longer: Why Experts Say It's Safer (UK)

descendants.text: Rear-facing car seats: why the direction matters https://babysorted.com/article?slug=rear-facing-car-seat-guide

th.text:
Why keep your child rear-facing for longer?
A baby's head is about 25% of their body weight. An adult's is about 6%. In a frontal crash, a rear-facing seat spreads the force across the back, neck and head.
By law, R129 seats stay rear-facing until over 15 months. That's the minimum. RoSPA says keep going as long as your seat allows. And bent or crossed legs are fine.
Source: RoSPA and GOV.UK

L1.topic: Lunch extra: storing expressed breast milk (topics #4/#16)

pin.text: Fridge at 4°C or lower: up to 8 days, at the back, not the door. Ice compartment: 2 weeks. Freezer at -18°C: up to 6 months. Cool bag with ice packs: up to 24 hours. Defrost in the fridge, never the microwave, and use within an hour once your baby has fed from it. Compare milk storage bag prices from UK shops at BabySorted. Source: NHS.
mediaAltText: Baby held close in a parent's arms above five breast milk storage times with a milk storage bag, on mint.

pinterestData.pinTitle: How Long Does Expressed Breast Milk Keep? (NHS Storage Times)

th.text:
Expressed breast milk keeps longer than many parents think. NHS storage times:
1. Back of the fridge at 4°C or lower: up to 8 days.
2. Ice compartment of the fridge: 2 weeks.
3. Freezer at -18°C or lower: up to 6 months.
Defrost it slowly in the fridge, never in the microwave. Once your baby has drunk from a bottle, use it within 1 hour, then throw the rest away.
Source: NHS

L2.topic: Lunch extra: fitting a car seat with the seat belt (topic #24)

pin.text: Belt-fitted seats can be just as safe when fitted right. Thread the belt through every guide, avoid buckle crunch on the seat frame, pull out all the slack and follow the colour codes: blue guides for rear-facing, red for forward-facing on R44 seats. Compare car seat prices from UK shops at BabySorted. Source: RoSPA, the UK accident prevention charity.
mediaAltText: Mum sitting on the floor smiling at her baby above four seat belt fitting checks with a grey car seat, on white.

pinterestData.pinTitle: Fitting a Car Seat With the Seat Belt: 4 Checks (UK)

th.text:
Fitting a car seat with the adult seat belt? Three checks:
1. Thread the belt through every guide on the seat.
2. Watch for buckle crunch: the belt buckle must not rest on the seat's frame. Only the webbing should touch it.
3. Pull out all the slack.
On older R44 seats the guides are colour coded: blue for rear-facing, red for forward-facing. i-Size seats use green.
Source: RoSPA
